title: Edge batch compression and deferred kernel selection to reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe intermittent 99.9th percentile tail spikes on hosted inference during bursty traffic (microbursts of many short requests and a subset of long-decoding streams). Current admission logic either accepts everything (causing GPU kernel contention) or throttles aggressively (high p99 but poor throughput). Goal: introduce a two-part runtime change: 1) 'edge batch compression' — opportunistically merge very short sequences into compact logical batches at the admission gateway to reduce kernel invocation overhead and improve utilization without increasing decode latency for long streams; 2) 'deferred kernel selection' — postpone final kernel path decision until more of the batch shape and KV-cache distribution is known (within a bounded window), allowing selection of a kernel optimized for the observed sequence length distribution and attention sparsity hints. This ticket covers prototype design, simulation, and an A/B experiment in staging.
acceptance_criteria: p99 end-to-end latency reduction >= 20% on synthetic bursty short-request workload compared to baseline admission
no >5% regression in median latency or throughput on steady-state medium-length workloads
deferred kernel decision does not add more than 1.5ms median decision overhead per batch
feature gated and toggleable via runtime flags and per-customer routing policy
design doc reviewed and signed off by infra and runtime teams
automated canary rollout with rollback triggers for latency and error rate

implementation_notes: Edge batch compression rules: only merge requests with input length <= 32 tokens and identical model variant and temperature seed; maintain request boundaries via offsets so post-decode per-request extraction is zero-copy. Compression must preserve deterministic RNG and stop-sequence semantics. Deferred kernel selection: the batch planner will start with a conservative default kernel but hold final kernel dispatch for up to 2ms or until batch shape stabilizes (whichever comes first). If timeout elapses, pick the best-available kernel for the current shape. Add telemetry for decisions: times held, final kernel chosen, fallback reasons.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: holding batches longer can increase latency for some requests — mitigated by strict 2ms bound and by exempting high-priority low-latency routes.
Risk: merging requests complicates per-request billing and observability — mitigation: attach compression metadata and expand in observability pipeline; billing team consulted.
Tradeoff: kernel warmup/opportunity cost — deferred selection improves match but can lose micro-opportunity windows; we will measure matched-kernel throughput gains vs decision overhead.
Risk: attention hint misuse — models may emit spurious hints; require conservative default and optional enforcement in kernel selector.
open_questions: Should compression occur only at edge (gateway) or be available inside dedicated pools?
What's the right default hold window for deferred selection on different GPU families?
How to expose per-customer opt-out if they require strict request isolation?
Do we need a generic API for other runtime optimizations (e.g., KV prefetch hints)?
